children: The Indian rupee opened with little change versus the US dollar on September 2, amid surge in oil prices and rising U.S. Treasury yields.
The rupee opened marginally higher at 94.92 per dollar, compared with Tuesday’s close of 94.95.

According to Finrex, the rupee is expected to open at 95.02 this morning, with the RBI keeping a close watch on the currency’s movement as Brent crude rises to $95.57 per barrel and the dollar index climbs to 99.77 amid renewed risk aversion following fresh fighting between the US and Iran. The escalation has heightened concerns over prolonged disruptions to crude supplies from the Middle East.
Market participants will closely watch the RBI’s stance on the rupee, particularly as higher Brent prices could prompt oil companies to step up dollar purchases.
Exporters should wait for appropriate levels around 95.25 to sell, while importers should look to buy on dips, it added.

Asian currencies traded mostly lower against the dollar, with the South Korean Won rising 0.27%. The Indonesian Rupiah fell 0.12%, while the Japanese Yen declined 0.08%. The Philippines Peso dropped 0.28%, followed by the Taiwan Dollar at 0.11%, Thai Baht at 0.08%, China Renminbi at 0.06%, Malaysian Ringgit at 0.05% and Singapore Dollar at 0.02%.
The dollar held firm on Wednesday as renewed hostilities in the Middle East pushed oil prices higher and revived inflation concerns.
The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies including the yen and the euro, was at 99.74.

title: Currency Check: Rupee opens with marginal gains against the US dollar
